bib.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

question: Can a sequence model scale linearly in length yet match Transformer quality on dense modalities such as language?
hypothesis: Making SSM parameters input-dependent (selection) lets the model filter and remember content, closing the quality gap that time-invariant SSMs have on discrete data.
contributions: Selection mechanism: Delta, B, C as functions of the input
Hardware-aware selective scan via kernel fusion, parallel scan and recomputation
Empirical results across language, DNA, audio, synthetics

method.summary: Mamba makes SSM parameters (Delta, B, C) functions of the input (selection), computes the resulting time-varying recurrence with a fused hardware-aware parallel scan that keeps the expanded state in SRAM, and stacks a single homogeneous gated block (H3 + MLP merged) with no attention or MLP. Evaluated on synthetics, Pile language modeling (125M-2.8B), HG38 DNA, and audio (YouTubeMix, SC09).

training.batch_size: 0.5M tokens (LM scaling); 1M tokens for 1.3B 300B-token run; DNA 1024 seqs (~1M tokens) size sweep, 2^24 tokens/step context sweep; selective copying 64; induction heads 8; SC09 16
training.steps: LM 4800/13500/29000/50000; DNA 10K (size), 20K (context); audio 200K; SC09 200000; selective copying 400K
training.precision: BF16 inputs in scan benchmark; training precision not stated

limits: Evaluation limited to sizes below 7B; authors say it remains to assess larger sizes.
Selection hurts continuous modalities such as audio waveforms (complex LTI S4 better).
Downstream affordances (fine-tuning, in-context learning, instruction tuning, RLHF, quantization) not studied.
No seeds, error bars or training hardware/compute reported.
Mamba-MHA hybrid only slightly better than pure Mamba at the scales tested.
